source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: Bucket flush
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a per-bucket Advanced Settings toggle that must be explicitly enabled before the bucket can be cleared of all documents while keeping its configuration; a bucket-level Capella management concept, not an Eventing-specific one

relations.subject: capella:bucket-flush
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for the flush operation's effect, distinct from a delete/DML statement because it resets the whole bucket rather than targeting matched documents
relations.evidence: Flushing clears a bucket of all documents and resets it to an empty state while maintaining the bucket's configuration and settings.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: The Function resumes from the checkpoint created when you paused it. It then executes on all new documents and on any mutations that occur after the checkpoint.

relations.subject: eventing:on-update-handler
relations.evidence: review[meta.id] = doc; // Saves the modified document for review

notable_absence.finding: Despite its title and this batch's hypothesis that a 'high risk patterns' page might reveal an Eventing-specific safety constraint or anti-pattern warning, this page's 'risk' is entirely a business-domain concept (flagging credit-card transactions that exceed a spending threshold or use a foreign currency) - there is no language here about Eventing execution risk, unsafe coding patterns, resource limits, or anything analogous to a platform-level safety gate. The only genuinely reusable structural finding on this page is the pause/resume/checkpoint mechanism (already minted by the sibling batch from manage-eventing-functions.md), which this page is the first worked example to actually exercise end-to-end rather than just describe.

cross_product_finding: The page notes an optional downstream integration point without documenting it: '(Optional) Uses custom applications written in a Couchbase SDK or a third-party integration like Kafka to read items in the `review` collection.' This is the first explicit mention of Kafka as an integration target anywhere in the Eventing worked examples in this batch, naming a third-party product boundary but providing no further detail or link.
